learning_outcomes.text: Know the main data preprocessing techniques and determine the most appropriate in each context.
Perform a principal component analysis and know the main methods.
Perform an exploratory and confirmatory factor analysis of a dataset.
Know the different multidimensional scaling methods and the differences between them.
Perform a correspondence analysis on a dataset.
Handle with ease the different concepts and methodologies within discriminant analysis.
Properly distinguish between all the above techniques and apply the appropriate one in each context.

syllabus_topics: Data preprocessing techniques. Motivation. Preprocessing tasks: cleaning, integration, transformation, reduction, and discretization of data.
Principal component analysis. Method based on correlations. Method based on covariances. Limitations.
Multidimensional scaling (MDS). Classic and non-metric models.
Discriminant analysis. Discriminant functions. LDA, incremental LDA, multiclass LDA, and high-dimensional LDA methods.

assessment_methods.method: Participation in forums and Campus Virtual activities

assessment_rules: The final grade in the ordinary call is calculated as: 0.05 * Attendance and participation + 0.10 * Forum and Virtual Campus activities + 0.40 * Practice evaluation + 0.45 * Final theoretical exam. There is no minimum grade required for any individual element. To pass the course, a minimum final grade of 5 out of 10 is required. In the extraordinary July call, students can retain their grades from the ordinary call. In the extraordinary January call, the evaluation will consist of a final theoretical-practical exam, which will account for 100% of the final grade. For differentiated evaluation, students can choose between the continuous evaluation system or a single theoretical-practical exam worth 100% of the final grade.
